newsitem.title: UK: Clyde holders want higher bid price - paper.
newsitem.headline: Clyde holders want higher bid price - paper.

text.p: Major shareholders of bid target Clyde Petroleum Plc are expected to refuse to sell their shares in the British oil company for less than 135 pence per share, the Independent reported on Thursday.

The newspaper, citing fund managers, said Clyde was expected to publish soon an estimate of its net asset value that would put a basic price tag of 105 pence on its assets, implying a possible bid price of 140 pence.
That price would represent a hefty mark-up from the current price of 105 pence offered by hostile bidder Gulf Canada Resources Ltd.
The Canadian oil firm has repeatedly refused to raise its 432 million pound ($715.8 million) offer, which was rejected by Clyde and criticised by some analysts as not being high enough.
The Independent said share ownership in Clyde was unusually concentrated, with just four shareholders controlling over 50 percent of its stock.
Clyde had until January 28 to produce its final defence document.
Clyde's shares closed at about 120.5 pence on Wednesday. ($1=.6035 Pound)
